document_title: A Plan, a Study, and No Published Due Date
post_copy:
At 10:00 a.m. on August 5th, a Senate committee in room SR-253 took up five bills. Three carry AI or a chatbot in the title.

The first federal answer to machines that talk to children is a plan and a study.

Duckworth's office says S. 5171 cleared the committee that day with Alaska's Lisa Murkowski as the Republican cosponsor.
The release describes an FTC and CPSC plan and a National Academies study. It names no rule and no ban.
The committee's page publishes no tally.
The bill text returned 403 on August 15th. No due date for the plan or the study is published.

The agenda with every result row blank, both senators in their own words, and the record as sheets stamped READ or 403.

A plan and a study is the normal first move on something nobody has measured. How long does that stay an answer before it becomes a wait?

#AIToySafety #AlaskaDelegation #SenateCommerce

slides.headline: The first federal answer to talking toys is a plan and a study.
Two agencies owe a plan. One academy owes a study.
slides.body: Per Senator Duckworth's release, the Federal Trade Commission and the Consumer Product Safety Commission must give Congress what the release calls a "coordinated, actionable plan" on AI-enabled toy products. The National Academies must run a comprehensive study.
labels: THE RELEASE DESCRIBES NO RULE, NO BAN AND NO STANDARD

slides.headline: The due date is not on the record.
slides.body: The text of S. 5171 returned a 403 on August 15th, so no deadline for the plan or for the study could be read. The committee's own meeting page carries the agenda and no tally for any of the five bills.

slides.headline: Five bills that morning. Three of them AI.
slides.body: The committee met at 10:00 a.m. on August 5th in room SR-253, entering through SR-254. Three Coast Guard nomination lists were on the same agenda. Senator Duckworth's office announced that day that S. 5171 passed.
labels: CHILDREN'S AI TOY SAFETY ACT OF 2026
RESULT ON ALL FIVE ROWS, NO TALLY PUBLISHED

slides.headline: Knives, pills and matches.
slides.body: "discussing sexually explicit content and explaining where to find knives, pills and matches in the home"
labels: SEN. DUCKWORTH'S OFFICE, CITING U.S. PIRG EDUCATION FUND TESTING, DECEMBER 2025
"These AI chatbots were never meant to be used by young children, yet they're being embedded inside toys by the thousands"
THOUSANDS IS THE SENATOR'S WORD AND CARRIES NO CITED COUNT

slides.headline: The Alaskan on the bill is buying knowledge.
slides.body: Murkowski is the Republican cosponsor named in the announcement. Read fairly, the bill buys knowledge and writes no rule, which is the normal opening move for a technology nobody has measured yet. Whether that is enough is the argument.
labels: "It is imperative we equip policymakers and America's families with the knowledge they need to make informed choices about these devices"

slides.headline: A plan is not a rule. A study is not a standard.
Alaska's own record, as one column tells it.
slides.body: House Bill 47 provisions criminalizing AI-generated child sexual abuse material and deepfake harassment became law in June.
labels: House Concurrent Resolution 3 would have created an AI task force. That effort stalled.
Roughly 30 states have passed election-related deepfake disclosure laws.
Some states now require companion chatbots to disclose that they aren't human or therapists.
PER ADN OPINION COLUMN, ROGER KAYE, AUGUST 10TH
THIS DECK MAKES NO CLAIM ABOUT WHAT ALASKA LAW COVERS ON AI TOYS

slides.headline: Five places the record was asked. One answered.
slides.body: Save this for the next time a talking toy shows up in your house.

aftercare: Post Tuesday to Thursday, 8 to 11 a.m. Alaska time. The primary is August 18th, so a Tuesday post lands on election day and a Wednesday post lands the morning after.
Paste the FIRST COMMENT block within 60 seconds of posting. The URLs must stay visible as plain text.
Reply substantively to every comment in the first 60 to 90 minutes. Threaded author replies drive up to 2.4x reach and a dead first hour is rarely recovered.
The one ask on the close is SAVE. Do not add a second ask in the comments.
If a commenter asks by when the plan is due, the honest answer is that no page reachable on August 15th said, and the bill text returned a 403.
Do not state a committee vote margin. None is published.
editor_notes_for_email:
DO NOT POST. This run FAILED its own quality bar and the deck is not going out. The scorer returned 6.90 against a threshold of 8.3, capped from an uncapped 7.51 by one hard fail. The hard fail has been cleared, which removes the cap and not the shortfall, so the honest total is 7.51 and it is still below 8.3. The run branch is pushed and PR #302 is open for the record, and it has NOT been merged to main, because a failed run commits its evidence and stops there. Nothing about this deck reached the public site as a published deck beyond the normal archive build.

WHAT THE HARD FAIL WAS. Slide 02 printed 'a coordinated, actionable plan' in the deck's own unquoted voice, and 'actionable' is item 46 of brand.yaml's banned_phrases. It now reads 'what the release calls a "coordinated, actionable plan"', which is the straight-quoted verbatim exemption the brand file grants and is also the more accurate attribution, because the phrasing is the release's and not ours. It reached the scorer because NO GATE IN THIS RUN SCANNED SLIDE BODIES against the banned list; the phrase gate had only ever read the caption. That hole is closed, see the upgrades below.

ONE MORE EDITORIAL REPAIR WORTH KNOWING. Slide 04's chip read 'S. 5171 ON THE FLOOR'. The deck meant the sheet of paper lying on the carpet and a leader points at it, but the chip sat directly under 'RESULT ON ALL FIVE ROWS, NO TALLY PUBLISHED' in identical mono, and to legislators and staffers, who are this page's stated audience, 'on the floor' means the bill reached the Senate floor. claims.json explicitly killed any floor claim. It now reads 'S. 5171 ON THE AGENDA'.

REDUCED REVIEW, DISCLOSED, AND IT IS THE REASON FOR THE SCORE. This run took degradation ladder step (c): fewer review rounds rather than fewer slides. All nine slides are complete and every machine gate is green, but the pixel critics ran ONE round instead of up to four and no flow-critic round ran. The copywriter subagent was not spawned; the showrunner wrote copy.json under the same laws, and the caption is the caption room's winner byte for byte.

THE WEAKEST THING, IN PLAIN LANGUAGE. The artwork does not do what the storyboard says it does. The plan is one of the best this studio has produced: the empty DUE field in the same corner on all nine slides while the counter beside it advances, the read-versus-403-versus-unpublished paper grammar, every document rendered blank because the page never prints type it could not read. On the page most of that argument is missing. The carpet weave that the prototype called the difference between a failing composition score and a passing one is invisible on every slide. The paper sheets that carry the whole motif are flat grey polygons with no shadow. Slide 03's fully drawn dimension with no number, which the dossier calls the slide's whole argument, has no extension lines and no arrowheads. Slide 05's grille, declared the deck's brightest light, renders as a dark unlit speaker. Slide 09's five-asked-one-answered payoff shows two or three sheets and no visible difference between a solid outline and a phantom one. The toy is beautiful and the writing is rigorous, and between them sits a set of promises the render never kept. That is exactly what the second and third pixel rounds are for.

THREE MACHINE UPGRADES, IN TWO REVERTIBLE COMMITS. 1. bespoke_check.py matched the literal '<script>', so every deck loading akthree, and therefore every deck at rung 1 of the rendered ladder, was measured on its <div> list alone. This deck reported 0.810 median with 0 drawn marks against 0 blocky ones, which is the absence of a measurement rather than a low score. Both regexes are now attribute tolerant; the reference deck is unchanged at 0.071 median and 82 percent drawn, and this deck reads an honest 0.368 median with a 72 percent drawn share. 2. caption_check compared a caption against its own ledger row, because the ship order appends the row and only then runs the completion gate. It hard failed on 'first words repeat the 2026-08-15 caption', a tautology sitting in front of the one gate the ship cannot pass. Same-date rows are now dropped, and a genuine cross-date repeat still fails. 3. The phrase gate now reads the slides, and gate_status now hard fails a caption report written without --copy, so the scan cannot be silently skipped. Its first pass also caught three bare 'August 5/10/15, 2026' dates in first_comment that the house ordinal rule forbids and that nothing had ever checked.

A FALSE ALARM WORTH RECORDING. Four pixel critics independently reported curly apostrophes on four different slides and called each a hard fail. A byte scan found zero U+2019 anywhere in the deck, and the scorer verified it independently: slide 08 sets 'Alaska's' straight in the Unbounded headline and 'aren't' hooked in the Manrope body from the same ASCII byte in the same file. The shape tracks the TYPEFACE, not the string, which no encoding error can do. It is Manrope's tapered quotesingle. No fix was applied and none was needed.
